title: Contrastive Cross-scale Graph Knowledge Synergy

problem.claim: Graph contrastive learning seeks to improve graph representations by gathering global information.

gap.claim: Single high-level graph views underestimate the complex and hierarchical properties of many real-world networks, resulting in sub-optimal embeddings.

contributions.claim: CGKS is a generic cross-scale contrastive graph knowledge synergy framework intended to improve generalization and awareness of latent graph anatomies.
The framework constructs a graph pyramid of coarse-grained graph views using a topology-aware graph coarsening layer that extends Laplacian Eigenmaps with negative sampling.
A joint optimization formula applies pairwise contrastive loss between coarse-grained graph views to promote cross-scale information sharing and knowledge interaction.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe the joint optimization formula containing pairwise contrastive loss between coarse-grained graph views as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on various downstream tasks reportedly show substantial improvements over the method's counterparts.

narrative_sequence.summary: Graph contrastive learning has received considerable attention.
Existing efforts emphasize a single high-level graph view and can miss complex hierarchical structure.
CGKS addresses the gap through a graph pyramid of coarse-grained views and topology-aware coarsening.
Pairwise cross-scale contrastive losses are jointly optimized to share knowledge and interact across graph views.
The authors report substantial downstream-task improvements over counterparts.

unknowns: Datasets, downstream tasks, evaluation metrics, baselines, and quantitative improvements are unspecified.
The graph coarsening procedure, negative-sampling configuration, and optimization details are unspecified.
No independent verification, ablation results, or reproducibility details are provided.
